ELUCIDATION OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BUKITTINGGI CITY

NUMBER 4 OF 2015

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The protection of women and children, until now, remains something that is widely discussed globally. There are still many, even in the most developed countries, violations of the rights of women and children continue to this day. The understanding or view of some communities that see women and children as parties of lower status, or under the dominance of men, until now still cannot be completely eliminated.

Recognizing this, in line with national development priorities, the Regional Government of Bukittinggi strives to produce local policies formulated within the framework of regional regulations, a guideline or reference for the empowerment and protection of women and children in a more institutionalized manner.

The objectives of formulating this Draft Regional Regulation are as follows:

1. To protect women and children from actions, decisions and policies that violate human rights.
2. To provide clear responsibility for the government, community, family, ninik mamak, and parents towards the rights of children and women.
3. To provide clear boundaries on the role of mamak to kemenakan and parents to children.
4. To protect women and children from acts of violence, neglect, exploitation, and human trafficking as well as the rights of women in the event of divorce.
5. To contribute to the realization of gender equality and justice in various activities and to improve the welfare of women and children in Bukittinggi City.
6. To organize the structure and institutions of government and customary institutions in efforts to protect women and children.
7. As a guideline in making policies for the Regional Government and social institutions in matters relating to the protection of women and children in Bukittinggi City.
8. To protect women and children domiciled in Bukittinggi City from actions that violate their basic rights.
9. To provide guidance on the role of the Regional Government, community, parents and other parties involved with the interests of women and children.

With the presence of this Regional Regulation as part of the national legal system concerning the protection and empowerment of women and children, all forms of violations of their rights such as being neglected, exploited, discriminated against and even often experiencing domestic violence (KDRT), low quality of life, inability to contribute to the progress of development, can be institutionally eliminated and eradicated in our region.

It can be affirmed that this Regional Regulation will later lay the basic rules regarding the authority, rights and obligations of the government, community and elements involved with children and women, by making local wisdom, customary values and the Minangkabau cultural worldview towards women and children as the main philosophical foundation, which can simply be expressed through customary expressions such as "bundo kanduang limpapeh rumah nan gadang", and "anak dipangku kemenakan dibimbing".

Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 35. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without using means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 36. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women, physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 37. Violence Against Children is acts of physical, sexual violence, emotional abuse and neglect of children as well as acts of exploitation and discrimination against children that make children sick physically and or psychologically, depressed, emotionally underdeveloped, feeling excluded and losing self-confidence. 38. Acts of Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the household scope. 39. Victim of Domestic Violence is a person who experiences violence and or threat of violence within the household scope. 40. Divorce is the release of the marriage bond from the husband's side by pronouncing a certain phrase such as "I have divorced you". 41. Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Empowerment Saayun Salangkah, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A Saayun Salangkah, is one form of service facility for women and children in an effort to fulfill information and needs in the fields of education, health, economy, politics and law, protection and prevention of acts of violence and trafficking against women and children in the City of Bukittinggi. 42. Child-Friendly City, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 43. Child-Friendly City Task Force, hereinafter abbreviated as Gugus Tugas KLA, is a coordinative institution at the city level that coordinates policies, programs and activities to realize KLA.

Article 4

Every woman has the right to:
a. Obtain protection from discrimination, exploitation (economic and social), neglect, cruelty, violence, abuse (physical, psychological, and sexual) injustice and other mistreatment.
b. Obtain equal opportunities and rights with men as human beings, in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social and cultural activities, defense and security and equality in enjoying the results of development.
c. For women workers:
1. obtain leave/rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months before the time of childbirth and 1.5 (one and a half) months after childbirth according to the calculation of an obstetrician or midwife, while still receiving wages or salary in accordance with applicable laws and regulations;
2. obtain leave/rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months in the event of a miscarriage while still receiving wages or salary in accordance with applicable laws and regulations;
3. obtain appropriate opportunities to provide breast milk to her child if this must be done during working hours, while still receiving wages or salary in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
d. Every woman who is married has the right to receive material and spiritual support from her husband.
e. Every woman who is left by her husband due to a divorce process must be provided with material support by her husband until there is a court decision in accordance with statutory regulations.
f. Every woman has the right to obtain decent work in accordance with her dignity and nature.
g. Obtain knowledge and skills that are useful for improving self-quality and family welfare.

CONCERNING

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE MAYOR OF BUKITTINGGI,

Considering:
a. that in order to guarantee and protect the rights of women and children so that they can participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and honor, and receive protection from violence, discrimination and violations, protection efforts need to be carried out; b. that in order for the protection efforts for women and children to obtain optimal results, there needs to be concrete action from the regional government and community participation; c. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a and letter b, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children; In View of:

Article 9

Protection for women includes:
a. Conducting socialization, education and anti-violence against women campaigns by actively involving all Regional Government Work Units, work partners and the community.
b. Ensuring gender mainstreaming programs in every Regional Government Work Unit, to guarantee equality between men and women, which is reflected in the Budget Plan of Regional Government Work Units.
c. Conducting early detection of cases of violence against women.
d. Providing service facilities for victims of violence against women, both services for physical victims and services for victims psychologically, through improvement of special facilities and facilities at Hospitals and at P2TP2A.
e. Requiring all Hospitals to be willing to accept women victims of violence for visum and undergo health care.
f. Providing women's rights in accordance with their dignity as women.
g. Protecting women workers from acts of discrimination, exploitation and violence.
h. Requiring the provision of special facilities and infrastructure for women according to criteria, in every government building, private office and other public facilities.
i. Requiring the provision of lactation room facilities for government buildings that provide public services and other public facility places such as malls, supermarkets, doctor's practice places and the like.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is the City of Bukittinggi. 2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the regional government and the regional house of representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 3. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Mayor is the Mayor of Bukittinggi. 5. Regional House of Representatives of the City of Bukittinggi, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution as an element of regional government administration. 6. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is one that has authority in the field of women's empowerment and family planning. 7. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and or community organizations. 8. Customs are eternal patterns of behavior passed down from one generation to another as heritage so that they are strongly integrated with community behavior patterns. 9. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter abbreviated as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business as a manifestation of community participation in improving the standard of living and welfare of the community with emphasis on voluntary service. 10. Social Organization is an institution/foundation/social association formed by the community whether legally incorporated or not legally incorporated that functions as a means of community participation in carrying out social welfare business. 11. Empowerment is a process, method and act of providing power and strength so that a person is able to explore potential and positive energy and have an impact on a better quality of life. 12. Woman is every person who is born, recognized by society and registered as a woman. 13. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily, develop themselves and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 14. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child still in the womb. 15. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children or father and children, or mother and children. 17. Household Scope is husband, wife and children, people who have family relations with the husband, wife and children, whether due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, and guardianship who reside in the household, and or people who work to help the household and reside in that household. 18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 19. Guardian is a person or body who in reality exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 20. Neglected Child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 21. Child with Disability is a child who experiences physical and/or mental obstacles that interfere with their growth and development naturally. 22. Toddler is a child aged 1 (one) to 5 (five) years, in the early stage of human development. 23. School-Age Child is a child aged 6 (six) to 18 (eighteen) years. 24. Delinquent Child is a child who behaves deviating from community norms, harming/endangering their own health/safety, disturbing the peace and order of society and family and community life, but still below the category that can be prosecuted by law/court. 25. Child Who is a Victim of Violence is a child who receives mistreatment such as being abused, humiliated physically, mentally and socially. 26. Child in Conflict with the Law is a child in conflict with the law and a child victim of a criminal act. 27. Economically Exploited Child is a child who is forced and deceived to be employed by parents or others without being paid or being paid. 28. Child Who is a Victim of Narcotics Abuse is a child who suffers from dependence on narcotics caused by narcotics abuse either of their own will or due to encouragement or coercion by others. 29. Child Trafficking is a criminal act or action that meets one or more elements of recruitment, transfer, handover of a child using violence or threat of violence, fraud, kidnapping, confinement, abuse of power, exploitation of a position of vulnerability or debt bondage for the purpose of and or resulting in exploiting the child. 30. Social Work Profession is a profession based on a framework of knowledge, values and technical skills and can be used as a vehicle in the implementation of social welfare business. 31. Child Care Center, hereinafter abbreviated as TPA, is a facility for guidance and welfare services for children aged 0-5 years whose parents do not have the ability and opportunity in child care, which is possible for playgroup services. 32. Playgroup is a child welfare business facility that prioritizes play activities and organizes pre-school education for children aged 3 years until entering basic education. 33.

Article 6

Every child has the right:
a. To live, grow, develop and participate reasonably in accordance with human dignity, and to receive protection from acts of violence, exploitation, discrimination and neglect.
b. To a name as personal identity and citizenship status.
c. To worship according to their religion, think and express themselves in accordance with their level of intelligence and age, under parental guidance.
d. To know their parents, be cared for and raised by their own parents.
e. In the event that for any reason the parents cannot guarantee the child's growth and development, or the child is in a state of neglect, then the child has the right to be cared for or adopted as a foster child or adopted child by another person in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.
f. To obtain health services and social security in accordance with physical, mental, spiritual, and social needs.
g. To obtain education and teaching in the context of developing their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.
h. To receive protection in educational units from sexual crimes and violence committed by educators, education personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.
i. To receive special and extraordinary education for children with disabilities and children who have excellence.
j. To express and be heard their opinion, receive, seek, and provide information in accordance with their level of intelligence and age for their self-development in accordance with the values of decency and propriety.
k. To rest and utilize leisure time, socialize with peers, play, recreate, and create in accordance with their interests, talents, and level of intelligence for self-development.
l. To obtain rehabilitation, social assistance and recovery of social welfare standards for children with disabilities.
m. To receive protection from treatment while in the care of parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for care, from discriminatory treatment, exploitation, both economic and sexual, neglect, cruelty, violence, and abuse, injustice and other mistreatment.
n. To be cared for by their own parents, unless there are valid reasons and/or legal rules showing that the separation is in the best interests of the child and is a last consideration.
o. In the event of separation between the child and their parents, the child still has the right to:
1. meet directly and maintain personal contact regularly with both parents;
2. receive care, maintenance, education and protection for the growth and development process from both parents in accordance with their abilities, talents and interests;
3. obtain living expenses from both parents; and
4. obtain other children's rights.
p. To obtain protection from abuse in political activities, involvement in armed conflicts, involvement in social unrest, involvement in events containing elements of violence, involvement in warfare and sexual crimes.
q. To obtain protection from being targets of persecution, torture or imposition of punishment or inhuman sanctions.
r. To obtain freedom in accordance with the law.
s. Every child who is deprived of their freedom has the right to:
1. receive humane treatment and placement separated from adults;
2. obtain legal assistance or other assistance effectively at every stage of applicable legal remedies; and
3. defend themselves and obtain justice before an objective and impartial juvenile court in a closed hearing to the public.
t. Every child who becomes a victim or perpetrator of sexual violence or who is in conflict with the law has the right to confidentiality.
u. To receive legal assistance and other assistance if they become a victim or perpetrator of a criminal act.

Article 3

The objectives of this Regional Regulation are:
a. To protect women and children from actions, decisions and policies that violate human rights. b. To provide clear responsibility for the government, community, family, ninik mamak and parents towards the rights of children and women.
c. To provide clear boundaries regarding the role of mamak towards kemenakan and parents towards children. d. To protect women and children from acts of violence, neglect, exploitation, and trafficking in persons as well as the rights of women in the event of divorce. e. To contribute to the realization of gender equality and justice in various activities and to improve the welfare of women and children in the Region.
f. To organize the structure and institutions of government and customary institutions in efforts to protect women and children.
g. To serve as a guideline in making policies for the Regional Government and social institutions in matters relating to the protection of women and children in the Region.
h. To protect women and children domiciled in the Region from actions that violate their human rights.
i. To provide guidance on the role of the Regional Government, community, parents and other parties involved with the interests of women and children.

Article 17

1. The protection of women and children is carried out in the form of protection:a. preventive;
b. repressive; andc. postremedial.
2. Preventive protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is implemented through socialization and guidance to parents, heads of families, housewives, guardians, teaching/educational staff, experts, caregivers (owners and officers of orphanages) and customary law communities about their obligations in the protection of women and children.
3. Repressive protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is implemented through law enforcement by law enforcers to establish and implement legal sanctions against people who violate certain rights of children and women.
4. Postremedial protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is implemented through efforts to provide assistance in law enforcement by lawyers, psychological guidance by psychologists and or religious leaders, and placement of victims in safe houses.

Article 23

1. Complaint Handling Services for violations of women's and children's rights are carried out by P2TP2A, PPA Units at Polres, Community Health Centers, Government Hospitals, and Legal Aid Institutions.
2. P2TP2A is established by the Regional Government.
3. The P2TP2A management is established by Mayor's Decree with a management period of 2 (two) years.
4. In carrying out its main duties and functions, P2TP2A is financed by the Regional Budget or other lawful sources.
5. Complaint Handling Services are conducted in the form of:a. reporters (victims or family, community and/or institutions) come directly, by telephone and/or letter to report acts of violence;
b. reporters are referred by NGOs, social organizations, the community or mass media; andc. in certain cases officers may visit the victim (reporter) directly.

Article 22

1. Violations of children's rights, whether in physical, psychological forms, discriminatory treatment, and exploitation must receive legal protection and be prosecuted legally.
2. In addition to the application of state law as referred to in paragraph (1), perpetrators of violations of women's rights may be subject to sanctions according to customary law that lives and develops in the midst of society.

Article 27

1. Every person who knows that a violation of women's and children's rights has occurred must report to law enforcement authorities the occurrence of such violation.
2. Every person, blood relatives, clan members, saparuik, tribe members, village members, or nagari members must report to law enforcement authorities if they know that a violation of women's and children's rights has occurred.

CHAPTER VIII

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION AGAINST

VIOLATIONS OF WOMEN'S AND CHILDREN'S RIGHTS

Article 20

1. Violations of women's rights, whether in physical, psychological forms, discriminatory treatment, and exploitation must receive legal protection and be prosecuted legally.
2. In addition to the application of state law as referred to in paragraph (1), perpetrators of violations of women's rights may be subject to sanctions according to customary law that lives and develops in the midst of society.

CHAPTER V

RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 11

The Regional Government together with the community is obliged and responsible to provide support for facilities and infrastructure in the implementation of the protection of women and children.

CHAPTER VI

SYSTEM FOR THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 16

1. The protection of women and children is implemented by upholding universal values stated in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
2. Bureaucratic restrictions must not hinder efforts to protect women and children.
3. Every parent, adoptive parent, guardian, teaching/educational staff, expert, caregiver at orphanages, and leaders of customary law community members are obliged to carry out obligations regarding the rights of children they care for and foster.
4. Every head of family, head of clan, head of tribe, leader, or other designation of customary law community leader is obliged to fulfill their obligations towards the women in their family, clan and tribe.

Article 24

1. Every woman or child who becomes a victim of violations of women's and children's rights is accompanied by a lawyer provided by the regional government in the context of case handling.
2. The costs of assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) are budgeted in the Regional Budget.

Article 5

Every woman is obligated to:
a. Respect each other, love each other and help each other with all family members and relatives.
b. Manage the household especially as a good housewife in accordance with local customs and her abilities.
c. Respect her husband and obey her husband as long as it does not conflict with religious values and customs.
d. Care for and educate children in accordance with religious values and customary norms.
e. Increase knowledge and skills that are beneficial for the family and community.
f. Comply with religious values and customary norms.

CHAPTER IV

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 8

The Regional Government is responsible for the implementation of protection for women and children actively.

Article 18

The protection of women and children must be carried out by parents, families, relatives, guardians, caregivers, teachers, the Regional Government, and customary law communities in the Region.

CHAPTER VII

IMPLEMENTATION OF SOCIALIZATION OF THE PROTECTION

OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 19

1. The Regional Government is obliged to conduct socialization and education regarding the protection of women and children by involving all elements of customary stakeholders, as well as universities and other community organizations in the Region.
2. Socialization and education as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the implementation of legal counseling, both through lecture methods, discussions, pamphlets, films, plays, randai, saluang, rabab, and other traditional arts.
3. Financing of programs and activities for socialization and education on the protection of women and children is budgeted in the APBD every year in accordance with regional financial capacity and laws and regulations.

CHAPTER III

RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Part One

Rights and Obligations of Women

Article 15

Families, caregivers, institutions and customary institutions are obliged to play an active role in providing the rights of women and children in accordance with religious and customary norms as well as applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 2

The implementation of Protection of Women and Children is based on: (1) Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

2. Basic principles of children's rights, including non-discrimination, the best interests of the child, the right to life, survival and development, and respect for the views of the child.
3. Universal teachings which state that women and children are a very important part in the context of the sustainability of a nation, not only viewed in religious principles, but in their implementation constitute human resources in the development of a nation.
4. The outlook on life and philosophy of Minangkabau customs as set forth in the teachings of Adat Basandi Syarak, Syarak Basandi Kitabullah; Syarak Mangato Adat Mamakai, Alam Takambang Jadi Guru, and Anak dipangku kamanakan dibimbiang, urang kampuang dipatenggangkan.

Victim of Domestic Violence is a person who experiences violence and or threat of violence within the household scope. 40. Divorce is the release of the marriage bond from the husband's side by pronouncing a certain phrase such as "I have divorced you". 41. Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Empowerment Saayun Salangkah, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A Saayun Salangkah, is one form of service facility for women and children in an effort to fulfill information and needs in the fields of education, health, economy, politics and law, protection and prevention of acts of violence and trafficking against women and children in the City of Bukittinggi. 42. Child-Friendly City, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 43. Child-Friendly City Task Force, hereinafter abbreviated as Gugus Tugas KLA, is a coordinative institution at the city level that coordinates policies, programs and activities to realize KLA.

Article 4

Every woman has the right to:
a. Obtain protection from discrimination, exploitation (economic and social), neglect, cruelty, violence, abuse (physical, psychological, and sexual) injustice and other mistreatment.
b. Obtain equal opportunities and rights with men as human beings, in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social and cultural activities, defense and security and equality in enjoying the results of development.
c. For women workers:
1. obtain leave/rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months before the time of childbirth and 1.5 (one and a half) months after childbirth according to the calculation of an obstetrician or midwife, while still receiving wages or salary in accordance with applicable laws and regulations;
2. obtain leave/rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months in the event of a miscarriage while still receiving wages or salary in accordance with applicable laws and regulations;
3. obtain appropriate opportunities to provide breast milk to her child if this must be done during working hours, while still receiving wages or salary in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
d. Every woman who is married has the right to receive material and spiritual support from her husband.
e. Every woman who is left by her husband due to a divorce process must be provided with material support by her husband until there is a court decision in accordance with statutory regulations.
f. Every woman has the right to obtain decent work in accordance with her dignity and nature.
g. Obtain knowledge and skills that are useful for improving self-quality and family welfare.

Article 9

Protection for women includes:
a. Conducting socialization, education and anti-violence against women campaigns by actively involving all Regional Government Work Units, work partners and the community.
b. Ensuring gender mainstreaming programs in every Regional Government Work Unit, to guarantee equality between men and women, which is reflected in the Budget Plan of Regional Government Work Units.
c. Conducting early detection of cases of violence against women.
d. Providing service facilities for victims of violence against women, both services for physical victims and services for victims psychologically, through improvement of special facilities and facilities at Hospitals and at P2TP2A.
e. Requiring all Hospitals to be willing to accept women victims of violence for visum and undergo health care.
f. Providing women's rights in accordance with their dignity as women.
g. Protecting women workers from acts of discrimination, exploitation and violence.
h. Requiring the provision of special facilities and infrastructure for women according to criteria, in every government building, private office and other public facilities.
i. Requiring the provision of lactation room facilities for government buildings that provide public services and other public facility places such as malls, supermarkets, doctor's practice places and the like.

CHAPTER VIII

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION AGAINST

VIOLATIONS OF WOMEN'S AND CHILDREN'S RIGHTS

Article 20

1. Violations of women's rights, whether in physical, psychological forms, discriminatory treatment, and exploitation must receive legal protection and be prosecuted legally.
2. In addition to the application of state law as referred to in paragraph (1), perpetrators of violations of women's rights may be subject to sanctions according to customary law that lives and develops in the midst of society.

Article 22

1. Violations of children's rights, whether in physical, psychological forms, discriminatory treatment, and exploitation must receive legal protection and be prosecuted legally.
2. In addition to the application of state law as referred to in paragraph (1), perpetrators of violations of women's rights may be subject to sanctions according to customary law that lives and develops in the midst of society.

Article 3

The objectives of this Regional Regulation are:
a. To protect women and children from actions, decisions and policies that violate human rights. b. To provide clear responsibility for the government, community, family, ninik mamak and parents towards the rights of children and women.
c. To provide clear boundaries regarding the role of mamak towards kemenakan and parents towards children. d. To protect women and children from acts of violence, neglect, exploitation, and trafficking in persons as well as the rights of women in the event of divorce. e. To contribute to the realization of gender equality and justice in various activities and to improve the welfare of women and children in the Region.
f. To organize the structure and institutions of government and customary institutions in efforts to protect women and children.
g. To serve as a guideline in making policies for the Regional Government and social institutions in matters relating to the protection of women and children in the Region.
h. To protect women and children domiciled in the Region from actions that violate their human rights.
i. To provide guidance on the role of the Regional Government, community, parents and other parties involved with the interests of women and children.

Article 27

1. Every person who knows that a violation of women's and children's rights has occurred must report to law enforcement authorities the occurrence of such violation.
2. Every person, blood relatives, clan members, saparuik, tribe members, village members, or nagari members must report to law enforcement authorities if they know that a violation of women's and children's rights has occurred.

Article 17

1. The protection of women and children is carried out in the form of protection:a. preventive;
b. repressive; andc. postremedial.
2. Preventive protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is implemented through socialization and guidance to parents, heads of families, housewives, guardians, teaching/educational staff, experts, caregivers (owners and officers of orphanages) and customary law communities about their obligations in the protection of women and children.
3. Repressive protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is implemented through law enforcement by law enforcers to establish and implement legal sanctions against people who violate certain rights of children and women.
4. Postremedial protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is implemented through efforts to provide assistance in law enforcement by lawyers, psychological guidance by psychologists and or religious leaders, and placement of victims in safe houses.

Article 23

1. Complaint Handling Services for violations of women's and children's rights are carried out by P2TP2A, PPA Units at Polres, Community Health Centers, Government Hospitals, and Legal Aid Institutions.
2. P2TP2A is established by the Regional Government.
3. The P2TP2A management is established by Mayor's Decree with a management period of 2 (two) years.
4. In carrying out its main duties and functions, P2TP2A is financed by the Regional Budget or other lawful sources.
5. Complaint Handling Services are conducted in the form of:a. reporters (victims or family, community and/or institutions) come directly, by telephone and/or letter to report acts of violence;
b. reporters are referred by NGOs, social organizations, the community or mass media; andc. in certain cases officers may visit the victim (reporter) directly.

ELUCIDATION OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BUKITTINGGI CITY

NUMBER 4 OF 2015

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The protection of women and children, until now, remains something that is widely discussed globally. There are still many, even in the most developed countries, violations of the rights of women and children continue to this day. The understanding or view of some communities that see women and children as parties of lower status, or under the dominance of men, until now still cannot be completely eliminated.

Recognizing this, in line with national development priorities, the Regional Government of Bukittinggi strives to produce local policies formulated within the framework of regional regulations, a guideline or reference for the empowerment and protection of women and children in a more institutionalized manner.

The objectives of formulating this Draft Regional Regulation are as follows:

1. To protect women and children from actions, decisions and policies that violate human rights.
2. To provide clear responsibility for the government, community, family, ninik mamak, and parents towards the rights of children and women.
3. To provide clear boundaries on the role of mamak to kemenakan and parents to children.
4. To protect women and children from acts of violence, neglect, exploitation, and human trafficking as well as the rights of women in the event of divorce.
5. To contribute to the realization of gender equality and justice in various activities and to improve the welfare of women and children in Bukittinggi City.
6. To organize the structure and institutions of government and customary institutions in efforts to protect women and children.
7. As a guideline in making policies for the Regional Government and social institutions in matters relating to the protection of women and children in Bukittinggi City.
8. To protect women and children domiciled in Bukittinggi City from actions that violate their basic rights.
9. To provide guidance on the role of the Regional Government, community, parents and other parties involved with the interests of women and children.

With the presence of this Regional Regulation as part of the national legal system concerning the protection and empowerment of women and children, all forms of violations of their rights such as being neglected, exploited, discriminated against and even often experiencing domestic violence (KDRT), low quality of life, inability to contribute to the progress of development, can be institutionally eliminated and eradicated in our region.

It can be affirmed that this Regional Regulation will later lay the basic rules regarding the authority, rights and obligations of the government, community and elements involved with children and women, by making local wisdom, customary values and the Minangkabau cultural worldview towards women and children as the main philosophical foundation, which can simply be expressed through customary expressions such as "bundo kanduang limpapeh rumah nan gadang", and "anak dipangku kemenakan dibimbing".

CHAPTER VI

SYSTEM FOR THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 16

1. The protection of women and children is implemented by upholding universal values stated in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
2. Bureaucratic restrictions must not hinder efforts to protect women and children.
3. Every parent, adoptive parent, guardian, teaching/educational staff, expert, caregiver at orphanages, and leaders of customary law community members are obliged to carry out obligations regarding the rights of children they care for and foster.
4. Every head of family, head of clan, head of tribe, leader, or other designation of customary law community leader is obliged to fulfill their obligations towards the women in their family, clan and tribe.

CHAPTER V

RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 11

The Regional Government together with the community is obliged and responsible to provide support for facilities and infrastructure in the implementation of the protection of women and children.

Article 24

1. Every woman or child who becomes a victim of violations of women's and children's rights is accompanied by a lawyer provided by the regional government in the context of case handling.
2. The costs of assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) are budgeted in the Regional Budget.

CHAPTER IV

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 8

The Regional Government is responsible for the implementation of protection for women and children actively.

CHAPTER III

RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Part One

Rights and Obligations of Women

Article 18

The protection of women and children must be carried out by parents, families, relatives, guardians, caregivers, teachers, the Regional Government, and customary law communities in the Region.

CHAPTER VII

IMPLEMENTATION OF SOCIALIZATION OF THE PROTECTION

OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 19

1. The Regional Government is obliged to conduct socialization and education regarding the protection of women and children by involving all elements of customary stakeholders, as well as universities and other community organizations in the Region.
2. Socialization and education as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the implementation of legal counseling, both through lecture methods, discussions, pamphlets, films, plays, randai, saluang, rabab, and other traditional arts.
3. Financing of programs and activities for socialization and education on the protection of women and children is budgeted in the APBD every year in accordance with regional financial capacity and laws and regulations.

Article 5

Every woman is obligated to:
a. Respect each other, love each other and help each other with all family members and relatives.
b. Manage the household especially as a good housewife in accordance with local customs and her abilities.
c. Respect her husband and obey her husband as long as it does not conflict with religious values and customs.
d. Care for and educate children in accordance with religious values and customary norms.
e. Increase knowledge and skills that are beneficial for the family and community.
f. Comply with religious values and customary norms.

CHAPTER IX

IMPLEMENTATION OF HANDLING VICTIMS OF VIOLATIONS OF WOMEN'S AND CHILDREN'S RIGHTS

Article 26

Every woman or child who becomes a victim of violations of women's and children's rights in the context of rehabilitation is accompanied by a psychologist and/or clergyman at the expense of the government.

Article 25

Every woman or child who becomes a victim of violations of women's and children's rights receives free medical services at Community Health Centers, government hospitals.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BUKITTINGGI CITY

NUMBER 4 OF 2015

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The protection of women and children, until now, remains something that is widely discussed globally. There are still many, even in the most developed countries, violations of the rights of women and children continue to this day. The understanding or view of some communities that see women and children as parties of lower status, or under the dominance of men, until now still cannot be completely eliminated.

Recognizing this, in line with national development priorities, the Regional Government of Bukittinggi strives to produce local policies formulated within the framework of regional regulations, a guideline or reference for the empowerment and protection of women and children in a more institutionalized manner.

The objectives of formulating this Draft Regional Regulation are as follows:

1. To protect women and children from actions, decisions and policies that violate human rights.
2. To provide clear responsibility for the government, community, family, ninik mamak, and parents towards the rights of children and women.
3. To provide clear boundaries on the role of mamak to kemenakan and parents to children.
4. To protect women and children from acts of violence, neglect, exploitation, and human trafficking as well as the rights of women in the event of divorce.
5. To contribute to the realization of gender equality and justice in various activities and to improve the welfare of women and children in Bukittinggi City.
6. To organize the structure and institutions of government and customary institutions in efforts to protect women and children.
7. As a guideline in making policies for the Regional Government and social institutions in matters relating to the protection of women and children in Bukittinggi City.
8. To protect women and children domiciled in Bukittinggi City from actions that violate their basic rights.
9. To provide guidance on the role of the Regional Government, community, parents and other parties involved with the interests of women and children.

With the presence of this Regional Regulation as part of the national legal system concerning the protection and empowerment of women and children, all forms of violations of their rights such as being neglected, exploited, discriminated against and even often experiencing domestic violence (KDRT), low quality of life, inability to contribute to the progress of development, can be institutionally eliminated and eradicated in our region.

It can be affirmed that this Regional Regulation will later lay the basic rules regarding the authority, rights and obligations of the government, community and elements involved with children and women, by making local wisdom, customary values and the Minangkabau cultural worldview towards women and children as the main philosophical foundation, which can simply be expressed through customary expressions such as "bundo kanduang limpapeh rumah nan gadang", and "anak dipangku kemenakan dibimbing".

I. GENERAL

The protection of women and children, until now, remains something that is widely discussed globally. There are still many, even in the most developed countries, violations of the rights of women and children continue to this day. The understanding or view of some communities that see women and children as parties of lower status, or under the dominance of men, until now still cannot be completely eliminated.

Recognizing this, in line with national development priorities, the Regional Government of Bukittinggi strives to produce local policies formulated within the framework of regional regulations, a guideline or reference for the empowerment and protection of women and children in a more institutionalized manner.

The objectives of formulating this Draft Regional Regulation are as follows:

1. To protect women and children from actions, decisions and policies that violate human rights.
2. To provide clear responsibility for the government, community, family, ninik mamak, and parents towards the rights of children and women.
3. To provide clear boundaries on the role of mamak to kemenakan and parents to children.
4. To protect women and children from acts of violence, neglect, exploitation, and human trafficking as well as the rights of women in the event of divorce.
5. To contribute to the realization of gender equality and justice in various activities and to improve the welfare of women and children in Bukittinggi City.
6. To organize the structure and institutions of government and customary institutions in efforts to protect women and children.
7. As a guideline in making policies for the Regional Government and social institutions in matters relating to the protection of women and children in Bukittinggi City.
8. To protect women and children domiciled in Bukittinggi City from actions that violate their basic rights.
9. To provide guidance on the role of the Regional Government, community, parents and other parties involved with the interests of women and children.

With the presence of this Regional Regulation as part of the national legal system concerning the protection and empowerment of women and children, all forms of violations of their rights such as being neglected, exploited, discriminated against and even often experiencing domestic violence (KDRT), low quality of life, inability to contribute to the progress of development, can be institutionally eliminated and eradicated in our region.

It can be affirmed that this Regional Regulation will later lay the basic rules regarding the authority, rights and obligations of the government, community and elements involved with children and women, by making local wisdom, customary values and the Minangkabau cultural worldview towards women and children as the main philosophical foundation, which can simply be expressed through customary expressions such as "bundo kanduang limpapeh rumah nan gadang", and "anak dipangku kemenakan dibimbing".

Every woman or child who becomes a victim of violations of women's and children's rights in the context of rehabilitation is accompanied by a psychologist and/or clergyman at the expense of the government.

CHAPTER VI

SYSTEM FOR THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 16

1. The protection of women and children is implemented by upholding universal values stated in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
2. Bureaucratic restrictions must not hinder efforts to protect women and children.
3. Every parent, adoptive parent, guardian, teaching/educational staff, expert, caregiver at orphanages, and leaders of customary law community members are obliged to carry out obligations regarding the rights of children they care for and foster.
4. Every head of family, head of clan, head of tribe, leader, or other designation of customary law community leader is obliged to fulfill their obligations towards the women in their family, clan and tribe.

Article 27

1. Every person who knows that a violation of women's and children's rights has occurred must report to law enforcement authorities the occurrence of such violation.
2. Every person, blood relatives, clan members, saparuik, tribe members, village members, or nagari members must report to law enforcement authorities if they know that a violation of women's and children's rights has occurred.

Article 4

Every woman has the right to:
a. Obtain protection from discrimination, exploitation (economic and social), neglect, cruelty, violence, abuse (physical, psychological, and sexual) injustice and other mistreatment.

1. obtain leave/rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months before the time of childbirth and 1.5 (one and a half) months after childbirth according to the calculation of an obstetrician or midwife, while still receiving wages or salary in accordance with applicable laws and regulations;
2. obtain leave/rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months in the event of a miscarriage while still receiving wages or salary in accordance with applicable laws and regulations;
3. obtain appropriate opportunities to provide breast milk to her child if this must be done during working hours, while still receiving wages or salary in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
d. Every woman who is married has the right to receive material and spiritual support from her husband.
e. Every woman who is left by her husband due to a divorce process must be provided with material support by her husband until there is a court decision in accordance with statutory regulations.
f. Every woman has the right to obtain decent work in accordance with her dignity and nature.
g. Obtain knowledge and skills that are useful for improving self-quality and family welfare.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is the City of Bukittinggi. 2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the regional government and the regional house of representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 3. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Mayor is the Mayor of Bukittinggi. 5. Regional House of Representatives of the City of Bukittinggi, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution as an element of regional government administration. 6. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is one that has authority in the field of women's empowerment and family planning. 7. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and or community organizations. 8. Customs are eternal patterns of behavior passed down from one generation to another as heritage so that they are strongly integrated with community behavior patterns. 9. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter abbreviated as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business as a manifestation of community participation in improving the standard of living and welfare of the community with emphasis on voluntary service. 10. Social Organization is an institution/foundation/social association formed by the community whether legally incorporated or not legally incorporated that functions as a means of community participation in carrying out social welfare business. 11. Empowerment is a process, method and act of providing power and strength so that a person is able to explore potential and positive energy and have an impact on a better quality of life. 12. Woman is every person who is born, recognized by society and registered as a woman. 13. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily, develop themselves and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 14. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child still in the womb. 15. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children or father and children, or mother and children. 17. Household Scope is husband, wife and children, people who have family relations with the husband, wife and children, whether due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, and guardianship who reside in the household, and or people who work to help the household and reside in that household. 18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 19. Guardian is a person or body who in reality exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 20. Neglected Child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 21. Child with Disability is a child who experiences physical and/or mental obstacles that interfere with their growth and development naturally. 22. Toddler is a child aged 1 (one) to 5 (five) years, in the early stage of human development. 23. School-Age Child is a child aged 6 (six) to 18 (eighteen) years. 24. Delinquent Child is a child who behaves deviating from community norms, harming/endangering their own health/safety, disturbing the peace and order of society and family and community life, but still below the category that can be prosecuted by law/court. 25. Child Who is a Victim of Violence is a child who receives mistreatment such as being abused, humiliated physically, mentally and socially. 26. Child in Conflict with the Law is a child in conflict with the law and a child victim of a criminal act. 27. Economically Exploited Child is a child who is forced and deceived to be employed by parents or others without being paid or being paid. 28. Child Who is a Victim of Narcotics Abuse is a child who suffers from dependence on narcotics caused by narcotics abuse either of their own will or due to encouragement or coercion by others. 29. Child Trafficking is a criminal act or action that meets one or more elements of recruitment, transfer, handover of a child using violence or threat of violence, fraud, kidnapping, confinement, abuse of power, exploitation of a position of vulnerability or debt bondage for the purpose of and or resulting in exploiting the child. 30. Social Work Profession is a profession based on a framework of knowledge, values and technical skills and can be used as a vehicle in the implementation of social welfare business. 31. Child Care Center, hereinafter abbreviated as TPA, is a facility for guidance and welfare services for children aged 0-5 years whose parents do not have the ability and opportunity in child care, which is possible for playgroup services. 32. Protection for women includes:

f. Providing women's rights in accordance with their dignity as women.

CHAPTER VIII

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION AGAINST

VIOLATIONS OF WOMEN'S AND CHILDREN'S RIGHTS

Article 20

1. Violations of women's rights, whether in physical, psychological forms, discriminatory treatment, and exploitation must receive legal protection and be prosecuted legally.
2. In addition to the application of state law as referred to in paragraph (1), perpetrators of violations of women's rights may be subject to sanctions according to customary law that lives and develops in the midst of society.

Article 6

Every child has the right:
a. To live, grow, develop and participate reasonably in accordance with human dignity, and to receive protection from acts of violence, exploitation, discrimination and neglect.
b. To a name as personal identity and citizenship status.
c. To worship according to their religion, think and express themselves in accordance with their level of intelligence and age, under parental guidance.
d. To know their parents, be cared for and raised by their own parents.
e. In the event that for any reason the parents cannot guarantee the child's growth and development, or the child is in a state of neglect, then the child has the right to be cared for or adopted as a foster child or adopted child by another person in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.
f. To obtain health services and social security in accordance with physical, mental, spiritual, and social needs.
g. To obtain education and teaching in the context of developing their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.
h. To receive protection in educational units from sexual crimes and violence committed by educators, education personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.
i. To receive special and extraordinary education for children with disabilities and children who have excellence.
j. To express and be heard their opinion, receive, seek, and provide information in accordance with their level of intelligence and age for their self-development in accordance with the values of decency and propriety.
k. To rest and utilize leisure time, socialize with peers, play, recreate, and create in accordance with their interests, talents, and level of intelligence for self-development.
l. To obtain rehabilitation, social assistance and recovery of social welfare standards for children with disabilities.
m. To receive protection from treatment while in the care of parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for care, from discriminatory treatment, exploitation, both economic and sexual, neglect, cruelty, violence, and abuse, injustice and other mistreatment.
n. To be cared for by their own parents, unless there are valid reasons and/or legal rules showing that the separation is in the best interests of the child and is a last consideration.
o. In the event of separation between the child and their parents, the child still has the right to:
1. meet directly and maintain personal contact regularly with both parents;
2. receive care, maintenance, education and protection for the growth and development process from both parents in accordance with their abilities, talents and interests;
3. obtain living expenses from both parents; and
4. obtain other children's rights.
p. To obtain protection from abuse in political activities, involvement in armed conflicts, involvement in social unrest, involvement in events containing elements of violence, involvement in warfare and sexual crimes.
q. To obtain protection from being targets of persecution, torture or imposition of punishment or inhuman sanctions.
r. To obtain freedom in accordance with the law.
s. Every child who is deprived of their freedom has the right to:
1. receive humane treatment and placement separated from adults;
2. obtain legal assistance or other assistance effectively at every stage of applicable legal remedies; and
3. defend themselves and obtain justice before an objective and impartial juvenile court in a closed hearing to the public.
t. Every child who becomes a victim or perpetrator of sexual violence or who is in conflict with the law has the right to confidentiality.
u. To receive legal assistance and other assistance if they become a victim or perpetrator of a criminal act.

Article 22

1. Violations of children's rights, whether in physical, psychological forms, discriminatory treatment, and exploitation must receive legal protection and be prosecuted legally.
2. In addition to the application of state law as referred to in paragraph (1), perpetrators of violations of women's rights may be subject to sanctions according to customary law that lives and develops in the midst of society.

Article 17

1. The protection of women and children is carried out in the form of protection:a. preventive;
b. repressive; andc. postremedial.
2. Preventive protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is implemented through socialization and guidance to parents, heads of families, housewives, guardians, teaching/educational staff, experts, caregivers (owners and officers of orphanages) and customary law communities about their obligations in the protection of women and children.
3. Repressive protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is implemented through law enforcement by law enforcers to establish and implement legal sanctions against people who violate certain rights of children and women.
4. Postremedial protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is implemented through efforts to provide assistance in law enforcement by lawyers, psychological guidance by psychologists and or religious leaders, and placement of victims in safe houses.

Article 6

Every child has the right:
a. To live, grow, develop and participate reasonably in accordance with human dignity, and to receive protection from acts of violence, exploitation, discrimination and neglect.
b. To a name as personal identity and citizenship status.
c. To worship according to their religion, think and express themselves in accordance with their level of intelligence and age, under parental guidance.
d. To know their parents, be cared for and raised by their own parents.
e. In the event that for any reason the parents cannot guarantee the child's growth and development, or the child is in a state of neglect, then the child has the right to be cared for or adopted as a foster child or adopted child by another person in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.
f. To obtain health services and social security in accordance with physical, mental, spiritual, and social needs.
g. To obtain education and teaching in the context of developing their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.
h. To receive protection in educational units from sexual crimes and violence committed by educators, education personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.
i. To receive special and extraordinary education for children with disabilities and children who have excellence.
j. To express and be heard their opinion, receive, seek, and provide information in accordance with their level of intelligence and age for their self-development in accordance with the values of decency and propriety.
k. To rest and utilize leisure time, socialize with peers, play, recreate, and create in accordance with their interests, talents, and level of intelligence for self-development.
l. To obtain rehabilitation, social assistance and recovery of social welfare standards for children with disabilities.
m. To receive protection from treatment while in the care of parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for care, from discriminatory treatment, exploitation, both economic and sexual, neglect, cruelty, violence, and abuse, injustice and other mistreatment.
n. To be cared for by their own parents, unless there are valid reasons and/or legal rules showing that the separation is in the best interests of the child and is a last consideration.
o. In the event of separation between the child and their parents, the child still has the right to:
1. meet directly and maintain personal contact regularly with both parents;
2. receive care, maintenance, education and protection for the growth and development process from both parents in accordance with their abilities, talents and interests;
3. obtain living expenses from both parents; and
4. obtain other children's rights.
p. To obtain protection from abuse in political activities, involvement in armed conflicts, involvement in social unrest, involvement in events containing elements of violence, involvement in warfare and sexual crimes.
q. To obtain protection from being targets of persecution, torture or imposition of punishment or inhuman sanctions.
r. To obtain freedom in accordance with the law.
s. Every child who is deprived of their freedom has the right to:
1. receive humane treatment and placement separated from adults;
2. obtain legal assistance or other assistance effectively at every stage of applicable legal remedies; and
3. defend themselves and obtain justice before an objective and impartial juvenile court in a closed hearing to the public.
t. Every child who becomes a victim or perpetrator of sexual violence or who is in conflict with the law has the right to confidentiality.
u. To receive legal assistance and other assistance if they become a victim or perpetrator of a criminal act.

NUMBER 4 OF 2015

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The protection of women and children, until now, remains something that is widely discussed globally. There are still many, even in the most developed countries, violations of the rights of women and children continue to this day. The understanding or view of some communities that see women and children as parties of lower status, or under the dominance of men, until now still cannot be completely eliminated.

Recognizing this, in line with national development priorities, the Regional Government of Bukittinggi strives to produce local policies formulated within the framework of regional regulations, a guideline or reference for the empowerment and protection of women and children in a more institutionalized manner.

The objectives of formulating this Draft Regional Regulation are as follows:

1. To protect women and children from actions, decisions and policies that violate human rights.
2. To provide clear responsibility for the government, community, family, ninik mamak, and parents towards the rights of children and women.
3. To provide clear boundaries on the role of mamak to kemenakan and parents to children.
4. To protect women and children from acts of violence, neglect, exploitation, and human trafficking as well as the rights of women in the event of divorce.
5. To contribute to the realization of gender equality and justice in various activities and to improve the welfare of women and children in Bukittinggi City.
6. To organize the structure and institutions of government and customary institutions in efforts to protect women and children.
7. As a guideline in making policies for the Regional Government and social institutions in matters relating to the protection of women and children in Bukittinggi City.
8. To protect women and children domiciled in Bukittinggi City from actions that violate their basic rights.
9. To provide guidance on the role of the Regional Government, community, parents and other parties involved with the interests of women and children.

With the presence of this Regional Regulation as part of the national legal system concerning the protection and empowerment of women and children, all forms of violations of their rights such as being neglected, exploited, discriminated against and even often experiencing domestic violence (KDRT), low quality of life, inability to contribute to the progress of development, can be institutionally eliminated and eradicated in our region.

It can be affirmed that this Regional Regulation will later lay the basic rules regarding the authority, rights and obligations of the government, community and elements involved with children and women, by making local wisdom, customary values and the Minangkabau cultural worldview towards women and children as the main philosophical foundation, which can simply be expressed through customary expressions such as "bundo kanduang limpapeh rumah nan gadang", and "anak dipangku kemenakan dibimbing".

CHAPTER II

Article 2

2. Basic principles of children's rights, including non-discrimination, the best interests of the child, the right to life, survival and development, and respect for the views of the child.
3. Universal teachings which state that women and children are a very important part in the context of the sustainability of a nation, not only viewed in religious principles, but in their implementation constitute human resources in the development of a nation.
4. The outlook on life and philosophy of Minangkabau customs as set forth in the teachings of Adat Basandi Syarak, Syarak Basandi Kitabullah; Syarak Mangato Adat Mamakai, Alam Takambang Jadi Guru, and Anak dipangku kamanakan dibimbiang, urang kampuang dipatenggangkan.

Article 17

1. The protection of women and children is carried out in the form of protection:a. preventive;
b. repressive; andc. postremedial.
2. Preventive protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is implemented through socialization and guidance to parents, heads of families, housewives, guardians, teaching/educational staff, experts, caregivers (owners and officers of orphanages) and customary law communities about their obligations in the protection of women and children.

Article 6

Every child has the right:
a. To live, grow, develop and participate reasonably in accordance with human dignity, and to receive protection from acts of violence, exploitation, discrimination and neglect.
b. To a name as personal identity and citizenship status.
c. To worship according to their religion, think and express themselves in accordance with their level of intelligence and age, under parental guidance.
d. To know their parents, be cared for and raised by their own parents.
e. In the event that for any reason the parents cannot guarantee the child's growth and development, or the child is in a state of neglect, then the child has the right to be cared for or adopted as a foster child or adopted child by another person in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.
f. To obtain health services and social security in accordance with physical, mental, spiritual, and social needs.
g. To obtain education and teaching in the context of developing their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.
h. To receive protection in educational units from sexual crimes and violence committed by educators, education personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.
i. To receive special and extraordinary education for children with disabilities and children who have excellence.
j. To express and be heard their opinion, receive, seek, and provide information in accordance with their level of intelligence and age for their self-development in accordance with the values of decency and propriety.
k. To rest and utilize leisure time, socialize with peers, play, recreate, and create in accordance with their interests, talents, and level of intelligence for self-development.
l. To obtain rehabilitation, social assistance and recovery of social welfare standards for children with disabilities.
m. To receive protection from treatment while in the care of parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for care, from discriminatory treatment, exploitation, both economic and sexual, neglect, cruelty, violence, and abuse, injustice and other mistreatment.
n. To be cared for by their own parents, unless there are valid reasons and/or legal rules showing that the separation is in the best interests of the child and is a last consideration.
o. In the event of separation between the child and their parents, the child still has the right to:
1. meet directly and maintain personal contact regularly with both parents;
2. receive care, maintenance, education and protection for the growth and development process from both parents in accordance with their abilities, talents and interests;
3. obtain living expenses from both parents; and
4. obtain other children's rights.
p. To obtain protection from abuse in political activities, involvement in armed conflicts, involvement in social unrest, involvement in events containing elements of violence, involvement in warfare and sexual crimes.
q. To obtain protection from being targets of persecution, torture or imposition of punishment or inhuman sanctions.
r. To obtain freedom in accordance with the law.
s. Every child who is deprived of their freedom has the right to:
1. receive humane treatment and placement separated from adults;
2. obtain legal assistance or other assistance effectively at every stage of applicable legal remedies; and
3. defend themselves and obtain justice before an objective and impartial juvenile court in a closed hearing to the public.
t. Every child who becomes a victim or perpetrator of sexual violence or who is in conflict with the law has the right to confidentiality.
u. To receive legal assistance and other assistance if they become a victim or perpetrator of a criminal act.

Article 9

Protection for women includes:
a. Conducting socialization, education and anti-violence against women campaigns by actively involving all Regional Government Work Units, work partners and the community.
b. Ensuring gender mainstreaming programs in every Regional Government Work Unit, to guarantee equality between men and women, which is reflected in the Budget Plan of Regional Government Work Units.
c. Conducting early detection of cases of violence against women.
d. Providing service facilities for victims of violence against women, both services for physical victims and services for victims psychologically, through improvement of special facilities and facilities at Hospitals and at P2TP2A.
e. Requiring all Hospitals to be willing to accept women victims of violence for visum and undergo health care.
f. Providing women's rights in accordance with their dignity as women.
g. Protecting women workers from acts of discrimination, exploitation and violence.
h. Requiring the provision of special facilities and infrastructure for women according to criteria, in every government building, private office and other public facilities.
i. Requiring the provision of lactation room facilities for government buildings that provide public services and other public facility places such as malls, supermarkets, doctor's practice places and the like.

Article 3

The objectives of this Regional Regulation are:
a. To protect women and children from actions, decisions and policies that violate human rights. b. To provide clear responsibility for the government, community, family, ninik mamak and parents towards the rights of children and women.
c. To provide clear boundaries regarding the role of mamak towards kemenakan and parents towards children. d. To protect women and children from acts of violence, neglect, exploitation, and trafficking in persons as well as the rights of women in the event of divorce. e. To contribute to the realization of gender equality and justice in various activities and to improve the welfare of women and children in the Region.
f. To organize the structure and institutions of government and customary institutions in efforts to protect women and children.
g. To serve as a guideline in making policies for the Regional Government and social institutions in matters relating to the protection of women and children in the Region.
h. To protect women and children domiciled in the Region from actions that violate their human rights.
i. To provide guidance on the role of the Regional Government, community, parents and other parties involved with the interests of women and children.

1. Violations of children's rights, whether in physical, psychological forms, discriminatory treatment, and exploitation must receive legal protection and be prosecuted legally.

2. Every person, blood relatives, clan members, saparuik, tribe members, village members, or nagari members must report to law enforcement authorities if they know that a violation of women's and children's rights has occurred.

CONCERNING
